$comment: Vendor configuration. This file is the ONLY place the monitored set is declared;
no vendor list lives in source code. Copy to vendors.json and edit, or supply your
own at deploy time.
type: which adapter parses the feed.
statuspage  Atlassian Statuspage v2 summary.json (most vendors)
instatus    Instatus summary.json (page.status UP/HASISSUES)
google      Google appsstatus incidents.json
apple       Apple system_status_en_US.js
microsoft   portal.office.com servicestatus (CONSUMER services only)
okta        Atom feed
salesforce  api.status.salesforce.com product instances
concur      open.concur.com JSON API
sorryapp    SorryApp status.json
betterstack Better Stack HTML status page
scope (optional): restrict which components count, by group or exact name.
Without it, the vendor's own page-level indicator is trusted.
With it, only the listed components decide the status.
NOT INCLUDED and why: Freshdesk, Freshservice and Paylocity publish no public
machine-readable status endpoint (verified 2026-07-30 - Freshworks' Statuspage
returns 401 'page is inactive', status.freshworks.com is a JS shell, and
status.paylocity.com redirects to their login portal). They were previously
sourced from StatusGator, a third-party aggregator, which is no longer used.
A monitored row with no real data source reports health it never verified.
ADOBE is NOT included, and the reason is a hard limit rather than a preference.
status.adobe.com is a JS app; its real data lives at data.status.adobe.com
(SnowServiceRegistry 2.2MB, StatusEvents 5.5MB). Parsing those costs ~70ms of
CPU, measured - against a Workers FREE-plan ceiling of 10ms for the ENTIRE
collection run across all vendors. Adobe alone would exceed the budget 7x and
kill the run for everyone else. It becomes viable on Workers Paid (30s CPU).
SOCIAL / MESSAGING - what is and is not available (probed 2026-07-31):
Discord    Statuspage, 30 components                            INCLUDED
LinkedIn   Statuspage, 11 components (www.linkedin-status.com)  INCLUDED
Slack      publishes JSON but in its own format, not Statuspage; needs a
dedicated adapter before it can be added
Meta       metastatus.com serves HTML only - no machine-readable feed
X/Twitter  api.twitterstat.us returns 401; the feed is no longer public
Signal     status.signal.org serves HTML only
Telegram   no status endpoint resolves at all
WhatsApp   no separate endpoint; Meta does not publish one
A row with no real data source reports health it never verified, so the
unavailable ones are omitted rather than faked.
FRESHWORKS (Freshdesk, Freshservice, Freshsales, Freshchat, Freshcaller) is NOT
included. Probed 2026-07-31: freshworks.statuspage.io returns 401 'page is
inactive'; status.freshworks.com and every <product>.freshstatus.io page is a
JS app whose embedded __NEXT_DATA__ holds branding only. Live status comes from
public-api.freshstatus.io/v1, which requires an account context that cannot be
inferred without executing the page's JavaScript. No combination of subdomain,
account_id or referer headers returned 200.

vendors.$comment: Cloudflare publishes ~470 components, most of them edge PoPs. Routine re-routing in far-flung data centres is the redundancy WORKING, not an outage, so scope to the services group. Measured 2026-07-30: unscoped = 46 non-operational (false red); services only = 0.
vendors.name: Cloudflare

vendors.$comment: Uses the JSON API the Concur Open React app calls. Scrapes of the HTML page return an empty JS shell (audit finding H7).
vendors.name: Concur

vendors.$comment: Services live at GROUP level; leaves are per-datacentre instances. MIGRATION WATCH: Docusign is moving to health.docusign.com (a Next.js app whose embedded state carries only locale strings - status is fetched client-side, so it is not parseable yet). status.docusign.com still returns 200 as of 2026-07-31. When the old endpoint is retired this row fails closed to unknown with a visible warning - it cannot rot to green the way findings H6 and H7 did - so switch it when health.docusign.com exposes a machine-readable feed.
vendors.name: Docusign

vendors.$comment: Google publishes its product catalogue separately from its incidents feed; componentsUrl supplies the list so every product can be shown, with open incidents marked.
vendors.name: Google

vendors.$comment: Services live at GROUP level here; the leaf components are per-data-centre instances. Listing leaves would show infrastructure, not services.
vendors.name: Jamf

vendors.$comment: Services live at GROUP level here; the leaf components are per-data-centre instances. Listing leaves would show infrastructure, not services.
vendors.name: KnowBe4

vendors.$comment: metastatus.com is a JS app; data lives at /data/orgs.json, found in its bundle. Covers BUSINESS/DEVELOPER platforms only - Graph API, Marketing API, WhatsApp Business Platform - NOT consumer Facebook, Instagram or WhatsApp.
vendors.name: Meta

vendors.$comment: CONSUMER services only - Outlook.com, OneDrive, Phone Link, Teams Free. Exchange Online, SharePoint, Entra, Intune and Defender are NOT in this feed. The adapter labels the row accordingly and warns. Enterprise tenant health needs the authenticated Microsoft Graph Service Health API.
vendors.name: Microsoft

vendors.$comment: Services live at GROUP level here; the leaf components are per-data-centre instances. Listing leaves would show infrastructure, not services.
vendors.name: NetSuite

vendors.$comment: Okta runs on Salesforce Experience Cloud with no public JSON API (summary.json, index.json, history.atom and history.rss all 401). The page embeds its incidents as JSON and the adapter parses that. The previous FeedBurner Atom source returned 200 but its newest entry was 456 days old - a feed that reports healthy forever is the same silent rot as findings H6 and H7.
vendors.name: Okta

vendors.$comment: Instatus splits page state and components across two endpoints; summary.json carries only page.status. componentsUrl is advisory - if it fails the page status still decides severity.
vendors.name: Perplexity

vendors.$comment: Services live at GROUP level here; the leaf components are per-data-centre instances. Listing leaves would show infrastructure, not services.
vendors.name: QuantumWorkplace

vendors.$comment: Seismic publishes 54 region names and no groups - infrastructure with no service breakdown. componentLevel none suppresses the list rather than showing data centres as though they were services.
vendors.name: Seismic

vendors.$comment: status.signal.org is a ~650-byte static page whose entire content is one sentence. The adapter matches that sentence and fails closed on anything else.
vendors.name: Signal

vendors.$comment: Stormboard migrated from Statuspage to Better Stack; the old summary.json now returns HTML (audit finding H6).
vendors.name: Stormboard

vendors.$comment: Salesforce publishes Tableau as per-region instances with no sub-service breakdown; instances drive severity but are not listed as components.
vendors.name: Tableau

vendors.$comment: Services live at GROUP level here; the leaf components are per-data-centre instances. Listing leaves would show infrastructure, not services.
vendors.name: Zoom
